what_it_does: Task-based parallel programming lets developers express work as small units (tasks) that the runtime system can schedule across many processor cores. Before running a task, the runtime must figure out which earlier tasks it depends on — this dependency analysis can become a bottleneck when tasks are very small and numerous. One optimization is to recognize and remember repeated sequences of tasks (called traces) so the dependency work only has to be done once. Existing approaches require programmers to manually mark those repeated sequences, which is fragile and breaks when combining code from different libraries. Apophenia watches the stream of tasks as the program runs, automatically detects patterns by treating the task sequence like a string of text and finding repeating substrings, and memoizes (caches) the dependency analysis for those patterns — with no programmer annotation required.
